In the Kali yuga, settlements will have food on display for sale; twice-born ones will have Śiva as their stake; / women will be burdened by their hairdress.
Thus praised, the great lord Śiva, the benevolent one, said to the deities: / "I shall release your wives who are held captive by the demon Malla."
Having then examined the triad of verses, he declared with certainty the bondage: / "The release will take place quickly, O Rāma, there is no doubt."

Having heard the words of the sage, Rāma, accompanied by the sage and the monkeys,
swiftly set out to search for Vibhīṣaṇa.
He quickly entered the city named Śrīraṅga; / the kings residing there worshipped Rāma.
Honoured by them, he then said, "Where is that Vibhīṣaṇa staying?" / [They replied,] "O divine Śrī Rāma, we do not know this matter."
The scion of Kakutstha dispatched the monkeys to all directions; / having gone, the best of monkeys did not see him at all.
Then Rāma said to the sage, "Tell me afterwards about Śambhu." / Saying "So be it," the sage Śambhu, accompanied by Rāma and joined by twice-born ones,
went to the settlement of brāhmaṇas, saying, "Show him, as it is." / Being questioned there, those honoured twice-born ones showed him
the rākṣasa bound in an underground chamber with many chains. / Then Rāghava said, "O brāhmaṇas, what has he done?"
They said: "The slaughter of a brāhmaṇa: an aged, most excellent brāhmaṇa, / a twice-born man highly righteous, very old, emaciated, alone,
stood in a grove for meditation; going there, Vibhīṣaṇa / crushed the brāhmaṇa with his foot, and that brāhmaṇa was completely pulverized.
Hence Vibhīṣaṇa was unable to take a single step; / struck by us, the wicked one did not die even under fatal blows.
Therefore, O Rāma, by slaying this sinful soul, become righteous." / Rāma, overcome with doubt, spoke these words to the brāhmaṇas:
"My own death were better; how can my devotee be slain? / Kingdom and lifespan were granted by me, and so it shall be.
In the transgression of a servant, punishment is wished upon masters everywhere." / Hearing Rāma's words, the twice-born ones spoke this in amazement:
The twice-born ones said: / "Death is not approved by sages for one crowned [king], O Rāma; / deliberate with the foremost sages, Vasiṣṭha and the others, upon what is wholesome."
Questioned by Rāma, the excellent sages then declared the expiation: / "The unintentional killing of a brāhmaṇa, however, is removed by rites of expiation.
This unintentional killing requires expiation: / let that Vibhīṣaṇa give three hundred and sixty cows."
And those brāhmaṇas who bound him said to one another, "So be it; / we shall release that rākṣasa; let him perform the expiation."
Releasing the rākṣasa, the brāhmaṇas presented him to Rāghava; / Rāma did not address him directly, but spoke in passing:
"Having bathed and consulted the angered sages regarding the expiation beyond this, / with the consent of the twice-born, let the sinful rākṣasa look upon me."
Hearing this word of Rāghava, the sinful rākṣasa, / having performed the expiation declared by the sages, then approached Rāma.
Purified in soul by the expiation, he bowed to the delighter of the Raghus; / Rāma, smiling, spoke these words to him within the assembly:
Śrī Rāma said: "From this day forth, O scion of Pulastya, act after deliberation upon what is beneficial, / since this trouble befell us for your sake, O rākṣasa.
Be compassionate everywhere, since you are my servant." / Then all those sages, once the matter was settled by the best of Raghus,
said, "How did ignorance quickly overtake us?" / Śambhu said, "O brāhmaṇas, through the insult of brāhmaṇas, ignorance will go to destruction."
The ṛṣis said: / "This Rāma [lived] in the Tretā age, and so did all the Purāṇas, / while the Bhārata [appeared] at the end of the Dvāpara; how is this appropriate in terms of intellect?"
Sūta said: "The Purāṇas nevertheless exist under those names; / but the Purāṇas proclaimed by Vyāsa are only today, not otherwise.
Even today there is that rule and fruit in the hearing of a Purāṇa; / the Mahābhārata too is distinguished here as an omen.
Having honoured the first book alone, one should observe the determination, / or all the books are praised in determining the meaning.
All the characteristics such as verse previously mentioned apply here as well; / from the syntactic connection of verses one [meaning is known], or from intention another.
One should understand the meaning; there the intention is apprehended, / for indeed everywhere the ascertainment of a thing and so forth is only from the meaning.
Where a meaning is seen, there that verbal root is cited; / here the characterization of words is only from meaning, not falsely.
Therefore, no other meaning should be adopted anywhere by the wise."
